body.estimand_functional: For \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), \(\alpha\geq1\), and every \(\kappa>0\), \(\mathfrak R_n(\epsilon;1,\alpha,1,\kappa,L)\asymp_{\alpha,\kappa,L}r_{n,\kappa}+\epsilon^{2/(\kappa+2)}\), attained by \(T_{\mathrm{Lip}}\), where \(r_{n,\kappa}=n^{-1/2}\) for \(0<\kappa<1\), \(r_{n,1}=\{\log(en)/n\}^{1/2}\), and \(r_{n,\kappa}=n^{-2/(\kappa+3)}\) for \(\kappa>1\).

sampling_model.design: Known clean design \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^d)\), observed only through a full-record Huber mixture.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) observed records are independent draws from \(R=(1-\epsilon)P+\epsilon Q\).
sampling_model.overlap: The propensity vanishes only on the boundary \(x_1=0\) and has polynomial order \(\kappa\) with calibration in \([1/4,1/2]\).
sampling_model.outcome: The clean outcome is bounded in \([0,1]\); only its two conditional means are Hölder-restricted.
sampling_model.contamination: The law \(Q\) may jointly corrupt \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\), including by placing atoms on the clean null boundary.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The estimator knows \(d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L,\epsilon\) and the clean covariate design, but not \(P,Q,u,\mu_0,\mu_1\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Unbounded inverse weights can make a point-identified treatment-effect parameter irregular, with rates governed by relative tail behavior.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: thm:lipschitz-all-kappa derives the three clean overlap regimes on the present controlled polynomial-boundary class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Huber minimax lower bounds are governed by the clean risk and a total-variation modulus, while Scheffe tournaments attain optimal full-law total-variation rates.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: lem:lipschitz-lower-pair-all-kappa and thm:lipschitz-all-kappa give an explicit same-experiment collision and a scalar-functional attaining estimator.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Projection-based higher-order influence-function estimators attain optimal clean rates for missing-response means under low nuisance regularity.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: oeq:full-frontier only; the remaining robust projected correction is unresolved.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: An empirically estimated Gram operator yields a semiparametrically efficient clean higher-order estimator without smoothness of the covariate density.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: oeq:full-frontier only; contaminated high-resolution Gram estimation remains unresolved.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Density-power IPW and doubly robust equations resist outcome outliers under stronger overlap and require an additional correction to retain double robustness.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: thm:lipschitz-all-kappa separates full-record Huber corruption from outcome-only robustness.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: A second-order correction can match an ATE nuisance-product frontier in a clean hybrid smoothness and structure-agnostic model.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: oeq:full-frontier only; the solved one-dimensional theorem uses direct boundary reconstruction rather than a robust higher-order correction.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Bias-corrected trimming supports ATE estimation and inference under limited overlap and is implemented for right-heart-catheterization data.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: thm:lipschitz-all-kappa supplies a theoretical all-kappa corruption radius and trimming-scale benchmark, without asserting that the application is contaminated.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Low-rank structure permits data cleaning and causal inference under structured measurement error, missingness, discretization, and privacy noise with bounded propensities.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: thm:lipschitz-all-kappa treats arbitrary full-record Huber contamination under vanishing propensity on a different structured class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 3 constructs a trimmed bias-corrected doubly robust estimator from clean i.i.d. observations, and Appendix B, Proposition B.1 verifies its ATE-specific boundary conditions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: thm:lipschitz-all-kappa gives a present-class contaminated minimax phase diagram for a novel controlled polynomial-boundary benchmark. The two experiments are incomparable, so no published converse transfers automatically.

body.tldr: On the exact one-dimensional boundary class with Lipschitz outcome regressions and propensity calibration smoothness at least one, one total finite dyadic cell estimator attains the same-experiment minimax risk \(r_{n,\kappa}+\epsilon^{2/(\kappa+2)}\) for every \(\kappa>0\). The clean term is parametric below \(\kappa=1\), equals \(\{\log(en)/n\}^{1/2}\) at the elbow, and is \(n^{-2/(\kappa+3)}\) above it. The theorem proves that clean minimax functional rate and the contamination modulus are simultaneously attainable on this subfamily; the higher-dimensional or non-Lipschitz smoothness interactions remain open.

project_justification.gap: The clean weak-overlap literature does not provide a same-experiment minimax theorem when an arbitrary Huber contaminant may replace \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\). In particular, the Ma--Sant'Anna--Sasaki--Ura clean conditions and this exact known-design polynomial-boundary contamination experiment are incomparable, so their asymptotic results and converses do not transfer automatically. No located result gives the all-\(\kappa\) clean elbow together with the full-record contamination radius on this declared class.
project_justification.niche: The missing benchmark is a boundary reconstruction whose variance changes correctly across the integrable, logarithmic, and nonintegrable inverse-overlap regimes while remaining stable when all contaminating mass is placed in its lowest-occupancy slab.
project_justification.fill: The variable-width dyadic estimator has error envelope \(h^2+n^{-1/2}V_\kappa(h)^{1/2}+\epsilon h^{-\kappa}+\exp\{-cnh^{\kappa+3/2}\}\). Optimizing its explicit cutoff yields the complete one-dimensional phase diagram, and exact clean-law pairs plus Huber-neighborhood collisions give matching same-experiment lower bounds.

body.related_work: MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026 is the nearest clean-record comparator: its Section 3 estimator and Appendix B, Proposition B.1 operate under clean i.i.d. sampling, whereas the present benchmark permits arbitrary joint replacement of \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\). Its weak-overlap conditions and this exact uniform-design polynomial-boundary experiment are incomparable, so no published converse transfers automatically. KhanTamer2010 explains support-tail irregularity but not this controlled boundary class or its contamination phase. ChenGaoRen2016 supplies the Huber-neighborhood testing template, not the scalar ATE estimator that preserves the clean functional rate. RobinsEtAl2017HOEE, LiuMukherjeeNeweyRobins2017EmpiricalHOIF, and BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024 motivate the still-open higher-dimensional projected route under clean sampling. HaradaFujisawa2024 treats outcome outliers under stronger overlap, AgarwalSingh2022 assumes structured corruption with bounded propensity, and neither covers arbitrary full-record contamination at a propensity zero. SasakiUra2022ET and SasakiUra2022Robustate motivate trimming and boundary correction; the right-heart-catheterization analysis is a consumer of the theoretical benchmark, not evidence that its records are corrupted or that its parametric propensity belongs to this class.
body.interpretation: The overlap exponent controls the clean price through the summability of inverse treated-cell mass. When \(\kappa<1\), that sum is finite and root-\(n\) risk remains possible; at \(\kappa=1\), contributions from all dyadic scales accumulate a square-root logarithm; above one, the lowest retained slab dominates and produces \(n^{-2/(\kappa+3)}\). Corruption has a different balance: a boundary slab of width \(h\) amplifies adversarial mass by \(h^{-\kappa}\), so balancing it with Lipschitz boundary bias yields \(\epsilon^{2/(\kappa+2)}\). One bandwidth attains both terms, so there is no additional nuisance--contamination interaction penalty on this subfamily.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The direct cell argument relies on one-dimensional Lipschitz covariance bias and boundary reconstruction. For a boundary cell \(B=[h,2h]\), clean treated mass is of order \(h^{\kappa+1}\), so either point or diffuse contaminating mass \(q_B\) shifts its weighted contribution by at most order \(\epsilon q_Bh^{-\kappa}\); at \(h=\epsilon^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) this equals the squared boundary bias. In higher dimension or under other smoothness orders, preserving the clean projected functional gain requires robust high-resolution nuisance and Gram estimation that is not proved here.
body.honest_scope: The headline is the exact one-dimensional result for \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), every \(\alpha\geq1\), and every \(\kappa>0\): \(\mathfrak R_n(\epsilon)\asymp r_{n,\kappa}+\epsilon^{2/(\kappa+2)}\), with a total finite estimator, the \(\kappa=1\) logarithm, and matching same-experiment converses. The former quadratic theorem is retained as a corollary. The cases \(d>1\), \(\beta\neq1\), or \(\alpha<1\), their interactions, and their remaining equality-case logarithms are open. Fixed nonzero contamination leaves irreducible ambiguity; no claim identifies \(\theta(P)\) from \(R\), and no claim says the Sasaki--Ura application is contaminated or satisfies this exact benchmark class.
